messages:
anya: quick thought — can we fan out a lightweight telemetry event from the admit hook so bench + quality + runtime-metrics can consume it? worried about latency impact on the happy path. :thinking:

anya: idea is the hook emits a tiny event (no raw prompts, only hashes + sizes + perf hints) and we async fanout to topics. bench only pulls a sampled subset to trigger deeper runs.

derek: how big is "tiny"? also need to define schema. if we stick raw tokens even hashed, legal might freak. can we keep it to counts + tokenization fingerprint + model binary id? :eyes:

marco: agree on strict boundary — admit hook should only own minimal signal sync. heavy payloads must go async. propose event schema "admit.event.v1":
```
{
  'event_id': '<uuid>',
  'model_id': '<registry-id>',
  'binary_sha': '<sha256>',
  'token_counts': {'prompt': 24, 'response_est': 128},
  'heuristics': ['large_inputs', 'long_context'],
  'sanitized_flags': ['no_prompt_text']
}
```
marco: consumers can enrich that with traces when they decide to run bench jobs.

sophie: need to nail retention + PII redaction. anything with prompt text is a no-go. also surface whether this goes to Hosted or Dedicated telemetry stacks (kms/HSM concern). we should add a redaction step in the hook pipeline and document what fields are allowed. :lock:

ida: cost tradeoff — if bench is triggered too often this will explode. suggest two-tier sampling: always send a header event, then downstream sampling decides if full benchmark job is enqueued. lightweight prefilter example: check model size + recent-failure-rate > threshold -> schedule.
```
# pseudo
def should_bench(event):
  if event['token_counts']['prompt'] > 512: return True
  if recent_regressions(event['model_id']) > 0.05: return True
  return random() < 0.01  # 1% baseline
```

infra-bot: deploy: admit-hook v3.2 rolled to staging at 2024-07-12T14:02:01Z (sha: ab12cde). :rocket:

derek: for transport, kafka + tiered topics sounds fine. we should include a "canary" tag on events so Dedicated customers can opt out of public telemetry + instead fanout to their private topic. fallback when brokers backpressure: drop enrichment and only emit header with metrics.

anya: nice — two questions: 1) who owns the schema + versioning? 2) is there appetite for a small refactor where admit hook returns a sync ack and separately emits to a telemetry writer service? that would keep latency predictable.

marco: schema + versioning should live in eng-ml proto repo. I'll sketch a minimal proto and a compatibility policy: additive fields OK, consumers must tolerate unknowns. for the refactor: yes — introduce a TelemetryWriter interface with one method: write(event, destination). limit changes in admit hook to call TelemetryWriter.enqueue(event). PR would be small: add interface, wire in current writer impl.

sophie: sounds good. can we also add a short runbook: if bench backlog > X -> switch to sampled-only mode and escalate to runtime-oncall? keeps costs contained. I'll draft the runbook and RFC follow-up. :thumbsup:

anya: cool, next steps: marco to drop proto sketch, ida to prototype sampler, sophie to draft runbook + legal checklist, derek to sketch broker config + backpressure fallback. i'll open a follow-up RFC referencing this thread. thanks all. :party_parrot:
__notes: This thread is a single Slack conversation string per agents.md requirements. No title included.
